_about: Non-canonical chemistry this engine can recognise by name.
This is NOT the parameterization registry. Appearing here means the system can
identify the residue and say what would be required to parameterize it. It
carries no force-field parameters and confers no permission to score, simulate
or rank a proposal that uses it. That permission comes only from
torsion_scan_driver records what the torsion-scan stage scales with. Where the
count is a plain structural fact it is stated; where it depends on linker
length or macrocycle size it is null and the note says so. An invented number
here would become an invented parameterization cost downstream.

Aib.note: Two methyls on C-alpha. No side-chain torsion to scan, but the backbone phi/psi surface is the whole point of the residue and is not transferable from Ala, so the backbone scan is mandatory rather than optional.

Nle.note: Straight-chain butyl side chain. Closest canonical analogue is Met with S replaced by CH2, so charges are not transferable.

Cha.torsion_scan_driver: chi1, chi2; ring pucker handled separately
Cha.note: Saturated ring, so it is not a Phe substitute electronically despite the similar volume.

N-methyl.note: Adds no side-chain torsion but removes a backbone hydrogen-bond donor and shifts the cis/trans amide equilibrium, so omega must be rescanned per residue context.

D-residue.full_name: D-enantiomer of a canonical amino acid
D-residue.note: The one case in this catalogue that does not need new parameters. Standard force-field functional forms are achiral: bonded and non-bonded terms are identical to the L form, and the inversion is carried by the sign of the C-alpha improper dihedral. What must be verified is that the improper is actually set for the D configuration; a silently-L improper gives a molecule that is the wrong enantiomer and reports no error.

staple.full_name: hydrocarbon staple (alkenyl amino acids plus ring-closing metathesis)
staple.torsion_scan_driver: scales with staple span and olefin position; not a fixed count
staple.note: Two non-canonical alpha-methyl alkenyl residues plus the macrocycle formed between them. The macrocycle is the hard part: its torsions are coupled, so scanning them one at a time is not sufficient.

gamma-Glu.note: Glu connected through its side-chain carboxyl rather than its alpha-carboxyl. Atom types exist; the connectivity does not, so the linkage torsions are new.

OEG.torsion_scan_driver: three rotatable bonds per ethylene glycol unit; total depends on how many units
OEG.note: Small-molecule chemistry, so GAFF2/OpenFF territory rather than a protein force field. The gauche effect about the C-C bond is the term most often got wrong by naive fitting.

fatty-acid.torsion_scan_driver: chain length; a C18 diacid has many nearly degenerate torsions
fatty-acid.note: Individually easy torsions, but the conformational ensemble is large and the interesting quantity is albumin binding, which the torsions alone do not give.

beta-amino-acid.torsion_scan_driver: an extra backbone torsion beyond phi/psi/omega
beta-amino-acid.note: Changes the backbone repeat unit itself, so no canonical residue's backbone parameters transfer.
